title: Bug Report: mysqlctld panic v23.0.0-rc1
body:
### Overview of the Issue

mysqld panic 

### Reproduction Steps

We run docker `docker.io/mysql:8.0.36` 

```shell
exec $VTROOT/bin/mysqlctld \
          --db_charset=utf8mb4 \
          --db_dba_user=vt_dba \
          --init_db_sql_file=/vt/secrets/db-init-script/init_db.sql \
          --logtostderr=true \
          --mysql_server_version=8.0.36-Vitess \
          --mysql_socket=/vt/socket/mysql.sock \
          --socket_file=/vt/socket/mysqlctl.sock \
          --tablet_uid=$(cat /vt/config/tablet-uid) \
          --wait_time=2h0m0s
``` 

### Binary Version

```sh
docker v23.0.0-rc1
```

### Operating System and Environment details

```sh
docker
```

### Log Fragments

```sh
mysqld E1017 15:13:52.550903       1 metrics_cgroup.go:57] Failed to init cgroup1 manager: cgroup1 manager is nil
mysqld panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
mysqld [signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x68 pc=0x14229e0]
mysqld 
mysqld goroutine 2025-10-17T17:13:52.554079316+02:00 1 [running]:
mysqld vitess.io/vitess/go/vt/servenv.getCgroup1CpuUsage()
mysqld 	vitess.io/vitess/go/vt/servenv/metrics_cgroup.go2025-10-17T17:13:52.554116116+02:00 :126 +0x20
mysqld vitess.io/vitess/go/vt/servenv.init.8(2025-10-17T17:13:52.554134395+02:00 )
mysqld 	vitess.io/vitess/go/vt/servenv/metrics_cgroup.go:60 +0x21d
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
This appears to be caused by https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/pull/18282 

Looks like we'll have to better handle the the scenario where cgroups are not available at runtime.

Thank you for the bug report, @reporter !

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter from looking at the code, I would only expect you to hit this if you have the `--grpc-enable-orca-metrics` flag specified. Can you please confirm? 

We'll need to think about how to repeat this issue (to confirm the bug and the fix), which is not yet clear to me.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @reporter ok, that's unexpected. And we have not seen this in the CI so it's something related to your environment (although I can see where we're not handling the general case of having a nil value). I still need some way to know that I've fixed it... Would it be easy for you to test a patch?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: OK, so this will impact everyone and it's not fully opt-in via the new flag. That's because the failure is happening in the `init()` function: https://github.com/vitessio/vitess/blob/f0738d1d4cdb7e14353b60e72789d9a4cfe7829d/go/vt/servenv/metrics_cgroup.go#L43-L66

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
@reporter can you provide any information on your container environment? It's `mysqlctld` that's panicking, not `mysqld`. MySQL has no Vitess code in it (which is where the panic is happening). 🙂  

This will help me try and get a similar environment in place for testing.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Hmm, Debian Buster/10 has been EOL for over a year. We're definitely not testing with that and the images are built with Bookworm/12: https://hub.docker.com/layers/vitess/lite/mysql80/images/sha256-bbc14f2ba18d33712f9a9070c6fb1c92a5abe24cf4b7c8f8ce3ffc3900270a30

I wonder if that's part of the issue here (again, not suggesting there isn't a bug Vitess side)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: OK, I think the problem is that Debian 10 uses cgroups v1 by default and that path hasn't really been tested because "everything" has been using cgroups v2 for some time now. 🙂 I will try to reproduce the issue from there...

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I just wanted to note that k8s 1.24 has been EOL for over 2 years and Debian buster for over 1 year.  cgroups v1 is also no longer fully supported in k8s for over a year: https://kubernetes.io/blog/2024/08/14/kubernetes-1-31-moving-cgroup-v1-support-maintenance-mode/

So trying to use the latest of software X (Vitess in this case) in such an old environment may prove challenging. It's going to be somewhat challenging for me to even install Debian 10 to test this as you can't install it in Orbstack, there are no AMIs for it, etc. 

Anyway... back to trying to set up an environment to test this. 🙂

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 totally understable, it could be documented in the release note that Debian Buster is no longer supported.
